quest.title: Mineral Investigation Special Lecture
quest.description: There seems to be an event underway near Speranza...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Primogem x20, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, Speranza's busy today! What's everyone chatting about?

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: We're trying to decide what the most beautiful rock in Nod-Krai is. My vote goes to Moonfall Silver.

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: Since Auni's not here, I'll go for Icy Pebbles on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Then I nominate Rainbowdrop Crystals! They come in loads of colors, and you can even make weapons with them. They're way more useful than Moonfall Silver and Icy Pebbles.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Weren't you deciding on the most beautiful rock?

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Well... I don't think a rock that just looks good but doesn't do anything can really be considered beautiful!

dialogues.speaker: Lumi
dialogues.text: Ya-ho... Ya-hoho!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Actually, Moonfall Silver has quite a few uses too — although they're certainly not as common in daily life as those of Rainbowdrop Crystals.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: As it happens, during my investigation, I came across some interesting stories about clothes woven from Moonfall Silver...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Huh? No way! You can weave clothes out of rocks?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Hehe, so you find it hard to believe, too? Well then, you'd best sit up straight and listen close...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Clothes made of Moonfall Silver... Paimon's super curious, too! C'mon {NICKNAME}, let's stick around to hear this!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Once upon a time, there was a fae governor in Nod-Krai who was obsessed with rare trinkets and had a passion for dressing up...

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: This governor's advisors worked day and night, desperately struggling to find new and exotic clothes for their master.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Then one day, a young tailor dressed in black came calling. He claimed to have inherited the mysterious techniques of the golden realm, and that he could spin crystals that glow like the silver moon into thread for weaving clothes.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The governor was overjoyed. He promised to pay the young man handsomely if he would stay and make him clothes.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The young tailor requested a vast quantity of Moonfall Silver be delivered to his workshop and demanded that no one disturb him while he worked. Naturally, the governor agreed.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: When the scheduled time arrived, the governor found the workshop completely empty, with neither Moonfall Silver nor any clothing to be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Having eagerly anticipated his new clothes, he hurriedly asked, "Where did all the Moonfall Silver go? And where are the clothes you promised?"

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The young tailor raised his hands, and, as if he were shaking out a piece of fabric, said —

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: "See? I took the Moonfall Silver you sent me and wove it into this gown, as pure as moonlight itself — too pure, in fact, for a fool or an unremarkable man to even perceive."

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The governor asked his advisor how the gown appeared to him, to which the advisor responded by saying it was the most magnificent gown he had ever seen, just like real moonlight woven and given form.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The governor could not see a thing, but unwilling to admit he was either a fool or unremarkable, he did as the tailor bade and "put on" the "moonlight gown."

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: To show off his extraordinary new gown, the governor decided to parade it, and himself, along the busiest street in town. But as he did so, he heard a child with a conch at his belt shout out—

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: "The governor isn't wearing any clothes!"

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: It seems like our Mikko has guessed how this story ends.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: The tailor was a cheat. There are people like that in Nasha Town, too. I heard about this one lady from Sumeru who schemed a whole bunch of folks.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What happened to the Moonfall Silver?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Good question. According to the story, the young tailor was none other than Reed Miller in disguise.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: He traded the Moonfall Silver he took from the governor for Mora and gave it to the poor townsfolk. While the governor was parading himself through town, Reed Miller was enjoying the show from a nearby rooftop.

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: He really got around, huh... I've already lost count of the number of stories he's popped up in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... But if he was lying about the whole thing, then doesn't that mean there were never any clothes made from Moonfall Silver to begin with?

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: I believe there were, but the art of weaving them has been lost, with the only evidence now surviving in folk stories.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The tale of "The Fisherman and the Beast" also mentions a moonlight gown... But Mikko and Maisie are still too young for that one, so I'm afraid it'll have to wait.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Huh!? No fair...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. You sure know a lot of weird and wonderful stories, Ms. Linnea!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I have a lot of travel knowledge to share, too.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Indeed! I'm sure you've noticed by now — the world is so vast, with so many secrets yet to discover!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Even the things we think we know may well have unfamiliar backstories, like Moonfall Silver.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: The same goes for Rainbowdrop Crystals, in fact. Each region of Teyvat has its own unique minerals, and just like people from different nations have different customs, rocks from different places have their own distinct characteristics too.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: If you have the patience to listen, you may discover that even silent crystals begin to talk, sharing the stories they have etched into their memories.

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: And not just minerals — lifeforms, both ancient and new, are beautiful and unique... This world is filled with stories and mysteries of all shapes and sizes!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: In the instant when a mystery is touched by the light of understanding, countless new possibilities reveal themselves, and the whole world opens up!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Ah, s—sorry, I'm getting a little carried away...

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: Linnea gets like this when she's talking about things she's interested in.

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: If we ask "Ms. Linnea" what the most beautiful rock in Nod-Krai is, she's certain to say, "Every rock is beautiful in its own way."

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: So it's probably better if we ask you two to cast your votes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #The most beautiful rock... What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Icy Pebbles? Paimon wasn't expecting you to say that!

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: What about you, Linnea? If you had to choose only one rock that was the most beautiful...

response.speaker: Linnea
response.text: Uhm... H—How about we end today's lecture here?

response.speaker: Mikko
response.text: Whoa, Ms. Linnea's trying to dodge the question!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all that, you went with the obvious choice! Paimon thinks Moonfall Silver is the prettiest, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, so you agree with Mikko. All those different colors make them very pretty, that's for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uhh... Well, Paimon guesses it does look a bit like a rock... and it sure is pretty!

dialogues.speaker: Linnea
dialogues.text: Why don't we invite the Adventurers' Guild to host a Geological Beauty Pageant in Nasha Town...

dialogues.speaker: Jurva
dialogues.text: If that happens, we'll need to find a way to ban Dorota from attending...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Yeah, if she's there, she'll do whatever it takes to make Moonfall Silver win.

dialogues.speaker: Maisie
dialogues.text: B—But, you can't just ban people from taking part...

dialogues.speaker: Mikko
dialogues.text: Of course you'd say that, you're on Team Moonfall Silver!
